findings.explanation: The PR diff replaces a parameterized query (cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname=%s;", (db_name,))) with string interpolation: cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='{}';".format(db_name)). The db_name value is user-controlled: in postgraas_server/management_resources.py:130-133 the POST handler parses 'db_name' directly from the request body (parser.add_argument('db_name', required=True, type=str)), stores it in db_credentials (line 143), and passes it to current_app.postgraas_backend.exists(db_entry) (line 158) and .create(db_entry, db_credentials) (line 164). PGClusterBackend.exists (backends/postgres_cluster/__init__.py:26-27) forwards entity.db_name to pgcd.check_db_or_user_exists, and create_postgres_db (postgres_cluster_driver.py:32) also calls check_db_or_user_exists(connection_dict['db_name'], ...). There is no whitelist validation of db_name anywhere in the chain, so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. db_name = "x' OR '1'='1") into the SELECT. The same regression also affects the db_user query on the next line and the CREATE USER/GRANT/CREATE DATABASE statements in create_postgres_db, which the diff changes from psycopg2.sql.SQL+Identifier (safe quoting) to raw .format() string interpolation.

The flagged line executes create_role = "CREATE USER {db_username} WITH PASSWORD '{db_pwd}';".format(**connection_dict). Tracing the data flow: create_postgres_db(connection_dict, config) is invoked from postgraas_server/backends/postgres_cluster/__init__.py:11 (pgcd.create_postgres_db(connection_info, self.config)), and that connection_info is built in postgraas_server/management_resources.py DBInstanceCollectionResource.post() (lines 122-164), where db_name, db_username, db_pwd are parsed directly from the HTTP request body via reqparse.RequestParser (lines 130-133) with no validation or whitelisting, then passed to current_app.postgraas_backend.create(db_entry, db_credentials) (line 164). Thus user-controlled db_username and db_pwd reach the SQL string via .format() with no parameterization or quoting, enabling SQL injection (e.g. db_pwd = "x'; DROP DATABASE ...; --").
